claim_text: INC Ransom listed Boeing on its leak site on Nov 20
summary: Ransomware tracker ransomware.live logged a Boeing entry attributed to INC Ransom, discovered Nov 20 at 03:46 UTC (Nov 19, 10:46 PM ET).
detail: We did not visit the leak site. The listing is known through a tracker and through press. A listing is a claim, not proof of a break-in.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A tracker, Cybernews and PlayCISO each report the listing; Cybernews says it saw it on the leak site. The three do not share a source, but all depend on the gang's own post, so this confirms only that the post exists.

claim_text: The gang says it took 3.6 million files from seven production servers at Boeing Sikorsky Aircraft Support
summary: The post claims over 3.6 million files, 33 years of data and email archives from a Boeing-linked helicopter support unit at Fort Campbell, Kentucky.
detail: This is the gang's description, relayed by the tracker and Cybernews. Cybernews says it is impossible to independently verify the scope. The group also says the unit is a Boeing subsidiary; PlayCISO notes Boeing's own 1997 release called it a Boeing and Sikorsky joint venture, which matters for whether Boeing's own network was touched.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The tracker copies the post and Cybernews summarizes it, saying the claim cannot be verified.

claim_text: The gang released about 10 screenshots as proof
summary: Cybernews says the group had released just 10 screenshots of supposedly stolen data at the time of writing.
detail: Cybernews says its researchers analyzed the samples and think they may link to the support unit. That is the outlet's assessment, not a finding that the data is real.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cybernews describes the screenshots and what its researchers made of them.

summary: As of Nov 20, Boeing had made no public statement about the claim, and its newsroom has nothing on it.
detail: Cybernews said it had asked Boeing for comment and would update when it replied. We found no reply.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Boeing's newsroom, read on Nov 20, lists nothing about a cyber incident; its latest release is a Nov 15 aircraft order. PlayCISO reports the same check.

summary: Boeing's SEC filing list shows no Item 1.05 cybersecurity 8-K; its latest 8-K, from Oct 27, covers quarterly results.
detail: A company may judge an incident not material and not file. No filing does not show there was no incident.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: EDGAR's list of Boeing filings, read on Nov 20, shows the Oct 27 results 8-K as the latest; PlayCISO reports the same.

claim_text: Boeing's systems, or its helicopter support unit's, were breached
summary: Nothing public confirms any intrusion, which system it touched or what data left.
detail: The only support is the gang's claim and screenshots, which no independent source has checked. Extortion groups often name a large company for pressure.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Cybernews calls the scope impossible to verify, and PlayCISO says no one independent has checked the claim.

claim_text: The data shown is real and from Boeing
summary: No independent check of the screenshots or files has been published.
detail: Cybernews analyzed the samples but says it cannot verify them.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: Cybernews describes the samples and says their scope cannot be verified.

claim_text: INC Ransom is a known ransomware group with many leak-site listings
summary: INC Ransom emerged in 2023, and the tracker lists more than 1,000 entries for it, all of them claims.
detail: This is background about the group, not evidence about Boeing. PlayCISO also reports that an alleged INC and Lynx affiliate was extradited to the US on Nov 17.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: PlayCISO summarizes the group's history and cites other outlets for it.

claim_text: Boeing confirmed a separate cyber incident in 2023
summary: In Nov 2023 Boeing confirmed a cyber incident in its parts and distribution business after a different group, LockBit, listed it.
detail: This is a different incident and nothing reported links it to the 2026 listing.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: PlayCISO quotes Boeing's 2023 statement as reported by BleepingComputer; we did not read the original.
